title: Structural exploration with AlphaFold2-generated STAT3alpha structure reveals selective elements in STAT3alpha-GRIM-19 interactions involved in negative regulation.
authors: Mishra, Seema; Kumar, Santosh; Choudhuri, Kesaban Sankar Roy; Longkumer, Imliyangla; Koyyada, Praveena; Kharsyiemiong, Euphinia Tiberius
one_liner_zh: 该文利用AlphaFold2和同源建模构建STAT3alpha结构，并通过分子对接与MD模拟研究转录因子STAT3与GRIM-19的蛋白-DNA相关互作（STAT3为TF，但GRIM-19为蛋白抑制剂而非DNA），聚焦结合界面与热点突变，方法可迁移至TF-DNA互作建模。
abstract: STAT3, an important transcription factor constitutively activated in cancers, is bound specifically by GRIM-19 and this interaction inhibits STAT3-dependent gene expression. GRIM-19 is therefore, considered as an inhibitor of STAT3 and may be an effective anti-cancer therapeutic target. While STAT3 exists in a dimeric form in the cytoplasm and nucleus, it is mostly present in a monomeric form in the mitochondria. Although GRIM-19-binding domains of STAT3 have been identified in independent experiments, yet the identified domains are not the same, and hence, discrepancies exist. Human STAT3-GRIM-19 complex has not been crystallised yet. Dictated by fundamental biophysical principles, the binding region, interactions and effects of hotspot mutations can provide us a clue to the negative regulatory mechanisms of GRIM-19. Prompted by the very nature of STAT3 being a challenging molecule, and to understand the structural basis of binding and interactions in STAT3alpha-GRIM-19 complex, we performed homology modelling and ab-initio modelling with evolutionary information using I-TASSER and avant-garde AlphaFold2, respectively, to generate monomeric, and subsequently, dimeric STAT3alpha structures. The dimeric form of STAT3alpha structure was observed to potentially exist in an anti-parallel orientation of monomers. We demonstrate that during the interactions with both unphosphorylated and phosphorylated STAT3alpha, the NTD of GRIM-19 binds most strongly to the NTD of STAT3alpha, in direct contrast to the earlier works. Key arginine residues at positions 57, 58 and 68 of GRIM-19 are mainly involved in the hydrogen-bonded interactions. An intriguing feature of these arginine residues is that these display a consistent interaction pattern across unphosphorylated and phosphorylated monomers as well as unphosphorylated dimers in STAT3alpha-GRIM-19 complexes. MD studies verified the stability of these complexes. Analysing the binding affinity and stability through free energy changes upon mutation, we found GRIM-19 mutations Y33P and Q61L and among GRIM-19 arginines, R68P and R57M, to be one of the top-most major and minor disruptors of binding, respectively. The proportionate increase in average change in binding affinity upon mutation was inclined more towards GRIM-19 mutants, leading to the surmise that GRIM-19 may play a greater role in the complex formation. These studies propound a novel structural perspective of STAT3alpha-GRIM-19 binding and inhibitory mechanisms in both the monomeric and dimeric forms of STAT3alpha as compared to that observed from the earlier experiments, these experimental observations being inconsistent among each other.
abstract_zh: STAT3是一种在癌症中组成性激活的重要转录因子，GRIM-19特异性结合STAT3，且这种相互作用抑制STAT3依赖性基因表达。因此，GRIM-19被视为STAT3的抑制剂，并可能成为有效的抗癌治疗靶点。尽管STAT3在细胞质和细胞核中以二聚体形式存在，但在线粒体中主要以单体形式存在。虽然在独立实验中已鉴定出STAT3的GRIM-19结合域，但所鉴定的域并不相同，因此存在差异。人STAT3-GRIM-19复合物尚未被结晶。基于基本生物物理原理，结合区域、相互作用及热点突变的影响可为我们提供GRIM-19负调控机制的线索。鉴于STAT3本身是一个具有挑战性的分子，并为了理解STAT3alpha-GRIM-19复合物中结合与相互作用的结构基础，我们分别使用I-TASSER和前沿的AlphaFold2进行了同源建模和基于进化信息的从头建模，以生成单体及随后的二聚体STAT3alpha结构。观察到STAT3alpha二聚体结构可能以单体反平行取向存在。我们证明，在与未磷酸化和磷酸化STAT3alpha相互作用过程中，GRIM-19的NTD与STAT3alpha的NTD结合最强，这与早期工作直接相反。GRIM-19第57、58和68位的关键精氨酸残基主要参与氢键相互作用。这些精氨酸残基的一个有趣特征是，在STAT3alpha-GRIM-19复合物中，它们在未磷酸化和磷酸化单体以及未磷酸化二聚体中表现出一致的相互作用模式。MD研究验证了这些复合物的稳定性。通过突变时自由能变化分析结合亲和力和稳定性，我们发现GRIM-19突变Y33P和Q61L，以及在GRIM-19精氨酸中，R68P和R57M，分别是最主要的和次要的结合破坏者。突变时平均结合亲和力变化的相应增加更倾向于GRIM-19突变体，从而推测GRIM-19可能在复合物形成中发挥更大作用。这些研究提出了STAT3alpha-GRIM-19在STAT3alpha单体和二聚体形式中结合及抑制机制的新结构视角，与早期实验观察相比，这些实验观察彼此不一致。
